name: Jens Axboe
org: Linux kernel block layer maintainer; SUSE; Oracle; Fusion-io; Facebook/Meta
why_notable: Danish Linux kernel developer and long-time maintainer of the block layer. He wrote the CFQ I/O scheduler, blktrace, the fio benchmarking tool, the multi-queue block layer blk-mq (which gives NVMe drives roughly one hardware queue per CPU core so storage I/O scales with cores), and io_uring (2019), a shared-ring asynchronous I/O interface that lets a single thread keep deep queues full without a system call per request. His work is why modern Linux can drive millions of IOPS and why 'more threads or async, not more GHz' is the rule for disk I/O.
